$comment: Announced partners Scout should surface, with the source behind every expectation: 88 partners, 59 sourced from SDF pages (stellar.org and developers.stellar.org), 28 from the partner's own announcement, and 1 (Stellar Index) listed from its operator's own site, which is not an SDF partner. source.owner marks which. Built from the read-only 2026-11-11 partner coverage measurement (17 questions). Scored by scripts/eval/partner-coverage.ts with the pure rules in src/lib/partner-coverage.ts. Judgement calls live in `overrides`, each with its reason; everything else traces to `source.url` or `expectedNetwork.source`.

rubric.classes: well: the expected row ranks within k for the partner's first query, carries an expected type, a status the source allows, a website on a partner domain, and no network contradicting a sourced one. wrong: a row exists but one of those fails, it is found only by an alternate query, or a row with the partner's name holds another slug. research-only: no row, but the research top 5 for '<first query> stellar' holds the announcement URL or a document naming the partner. missing: neither. could-not-check: a read the class needs failed after retries; never counted as a miss.
rubric.status: source status live: the row must be Live. coming: anything but Live or Inactive. announced: anything but Inactive. Overrides may narrow this.
rubric.types: Expected types use Scout's types enum. RPC providers must carry RPC so the RPC filter finds them; indexers carry Indexer or Analytics as their product is; Scout has no Custody type, so custodians count when typed Infrastructure, Wallet or Security.
rubric.network: deployment.network equal to the sourced network passes; unknown is a depth gap, not a wrong row; the other network is a wrong row.
rubric.resolve: A depth check, not part of the class: /api/projects/resolve on the partner name, then each query, must return the expected slug.
rubric.domains: Domains ending in stellar.org check a row's website but never identify a row, since SDF-owned pages host many rows.
rubric.ratchet: A worse class, a check that worsens (pass, then unknown, then fail), a worse rank for the partner's own name, or a question that loses an expected partner is a regression. research-only and missing share one tier, so a move between them is reported, not failed. When a question expects more partners than k, only a smaller found count is a regression; a swap is reported.

21X.reason: The only research hit for '21X stellar' is a false positive ('a 21X increase in transaction volume', SDF Story of 2020), so only the announcement URL counts as research coverage.

Curve.reason: Research hits for 'Curve stellar' are elliptic-curve CAPs and docs, not Curve Finance, so only the announcement URL counts as research coverage.

The Graph.reason: No row is named The Graph; the StreamingFast row (the Substreams provider The Graph's Stellar support runs on) answers for it through the streamingfast alias. Its website is streamingfast.io, so the website check fails and the partner scores as a wrong row, as measured.

Securitize.reason: SDF calls the integration planned (2026-10-28); a Live row resting on site liveness of securitize.io carries no Stellar evidence, so Live counts as wrong until a launch is sourced.

Obsrvr.reason: The Obsrvr company row is typed Indexer; its RPC product row (Horizon-as-a-Service, withobsrvr.com, typed RPC) is a separate row, so Indexer on the company row counts as correctly typed.

Franklin Templeton.reason: The row's website is the partner's official product site, which counts as the partner's domain.

WisdomTree.reason: The row's website is the partner's official product site, which counts as the partner's domain.

Figure.reason: The row's website is the partner's official product site, which counts as the partner's domain.

MetaMask.reason: The row's website is the partner's official product site, which counts as the partner's domain.

Novatti.reason: Novatti, the AUDD issuer, has a company row (novatti, novatti.com) beside the AUDD stablecoin row (audd) that answers its own name; either row answers a question expecting Novatti, as the measurement's domain match counted.

Copper.reason: Copper is also a commodity word: the research top 5 for 'Copper stellar' includes an SCF submission listing copper concentrate deals. A mention counts only within 80 characters of custody, custodian or custodial, which keeps the three documents that name Copper the custodian.
